Programming allows tasks that would otherwise be performed manually to be automated.
Machine-level language is the language understood directly by the processor.
It is represented using binary values:
The processor ultimately executes instructions in this form.
The explanation given associates these values with electrical states:
These binary states are used to represent machine instructions.
. Why was programming directly in machine language difficult?
Machine language consists of long sequences of binary values.
As the number of operations increased, remembering and maintaining large amounts of binary code became difficult for programmers.
Assembly-level language uses meaningful symbolic names or mnemonics instead of writing every instruction directly as binary numbers.

. What is a high-level programming language?
A high-level programming language is designed to be easier for human beings to understand and use than machine-level or assembly-level languages.
A compiler is software that converts
high-level language instructions into machine-level language
process of converting high-level language into machine-level language using a compiler
process of converting assembly-level language into machine-level language using an assembler
A language processor is software that converts another programming-language representation into machine-level language.
. What is the difference between a compiler and an interpreter?
A compiler converts the program as a whole into machine-level instructions.
An interpreter converts and executes instructions
. Why was platform independence important in the evolution toward Java?
As networked computing became more important, there was a need for software built on one platform to work on another platform.
This created the need for a programming language that was both object-oriented and platform independent.
